small_guidance:
- The epilogue kernel is already memory-bound and tiny relative to the ConvTranspose3d cost (10.1ms vs 3.5ms baseline) — further tuning of BLOCK_SIZE/num_warps on the epilogue cannot close the gap. If staying small, try BLOCK_SIZE=1024 with num_warps=4 and add an autotune over {1024,2048,4096,8192} × warps {2,4,8}.
- Precompute bias broadcasted to `[1, C, 1, 1, 1]` once and use channels_last_3d memory format on the conv output so the bias load becomes a contiguous vector load along the inner dim.
large_guidance:
- The dominant cost is `nn.ConvTranspose3d` itself (baseline 3.5ms; current run 10.1ms means the torch convtranspose plus the epilogue is slower than baseline — the epilogue alone isn't the bottleneck). Replace ConvTranspose3d with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per `(N, OC tile, input-spatial tile)`, computing the outer product of `input[n, :, d, h, w]` with `weight[:, oc, kd, kh, kw]` and atomically adding into the output grid at `(d*stride - pad + kd, …)` with bounds masking. Fuse the bias add and `(2x+b)*x + x` epilogue directly into the final write so the output tensor is touched once.
- Alternatively, implement as a gather-style direct kernel: one program per `(N, OC tile, output-spatial tile)`, looping over `(IC, kd, kh, kw)` and gathering input at `((od + pad - kd)/stride, …)` with the divisibility mask. This avoids atomics and is usually faster on Ampere when stride>1, since most kernel taps miss. Bake stride/pad/kernel as `tl.constexpr` and use channels_last_3d so IC is the GEMM-K contig axis.
- Fold the bias parameter and the entire `(x+bias)+x)*x + x = (2x+b)*x + x` algebra into the conv kernel epilogue so there is exactly one global write of the output, eliminating the second pass entirely.
